posts.author: samueloliveira
posts.body: Hey guys! As the title of the post suggests, I'm considering the possibility of creating a simple Virtual Tabletop to play Tabletop RPGs, and yes, I thought about creating this in RPG Maker! Yes, I know, it's a crazy idea, but could I do something simple? I already researched a dice roller  and saw that there is a way to do this. My main question is regarding the visualization of the board and how players will place their own maps, images, sounds, etc. I know that many will tell me that it's crazy, that there are already good programs and platforms (and I have them all: Foundry, Fantasy Grounds, etc.), but I thought about creating something very simple using RPG Maker. I would like to know your opinion, especially those who have delved deeper into RPG Maker. Thanks!

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: You want to make a table top maker inside RPG Maker?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Which RPG Maker?
Your profile says you use XP - if you're dealing with an engine older than MV, your ability to modify the engine via scripts is limited. It may be actually impossible to do without hacking the executables.
Doing this via MV or MZ is possible, but...
samueloliveira said:
I thought about creating something very simple using RPG Maker.
Click to expand...
That's impossible.
RPG Maker has no kind of Internet or multiplayer connectivity built in, so by definition doing anything like what you're describing is going to be
very
complicated. It would not be simple at all.
I can't imagine any reason to try to do this instead of using any of the already-made programs out there. Or just sitting there with webcams and drawing stuff on a piece of paper that you hold up to the camera.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body: If you want multiple people to be able to modify the same common map, it will be easier to do it from scratch than in RPG Maker.

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body:
I don't think the words yet exist for me to articulate to you how good an idea this isn't.
Trust me when I say I *get* ambitious projects, and it's often a great idea to challenge yourself by imposing constraints via the engine you use. This isn't that. You're basically just trying to fit an elephant in the fridge here. The container wasn't designed for it, and it's too big to go in there.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
I put a map editor and event placer within my game (yes, like the engine's editor, you can even edit each layer of each tile of the map) but making an entire engine within the engine would be too much for me and would extend the dev time by years.
So yeah, I'm not going to knock the OP's dream but I'm already envisioning years of work and you could probably just build the entire engine from scratch at that point instead of being limited by RPGMaker.
